argument: The counter exchange must live in actual SVG text bodies: the source needs a closed letter, the remote target an open letter, and a relay needs changed position. A bridge line, color, or readout cannot substitute for changed forms.

With labels, readout, controls, hint, caption, and furniture hidden, the first field should read as one dense typographic body, not a clause plate, route rack, pressure loom, or decorative alphabet grid. After a reply, the changed source, remote opening, and relay movement must be findable in the letter geometry.

Pointerdown must only arm. A same-gap return must refuse; a two-gap bridge must commit. Enter, Space, and the offer control must provide the same deterministic path; Delete lifts the latest exact body and R releases the field.

v028 must leave v025's offer-and-reply clauses, v026's approach-and-withdraw sculpture, and v027's duration-pressure loom through a singular counter-field, a two-place gesture, and actual letter-body exchange.

little-critters is translated as situated reciprocity without animals, eyes, faces, paper, or head-turning imagery. A local letter cannot look back; a distant gap must answer by changing typography elsewhere.

Delete v028 if it is an alphabet poster, if pointerdown writes, if same-gap contact commits, if source/target changes are only color, if the relay is only a decorative bridge, if later replies forget the body, or if exact lifting fails.
